note: The clearest ICP exclusion in this batch, and it fails on the one criterion the stated definition spells out in plain language. The ICP quote reads 'It's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight and I hate working out.' This prospect weighed 250 lb, is 210 targeting fat loss, has not trained since high school football, has been sedentary for fifteen or sixteen years at roughly 2,500 steps a day, and holds a discounted membership at his cousin's gym that he refuses to use — 'I just don't like it. I don't like going... I don't like people either, I guess.' That is the exclusion criterion almost word for word. Good_to_great fails for the same reason: this is rescue, not optimisation, and the goal is a glycaemic marker, not a physique. Neglected_health fails on the severity test the criterion applies — a type 2 diabetes diagnosis with an A1C that peaked at 8.8 is a crisis, not a neglected corner. He does meet the two commercial criteria. Successful is met on the equivalence test: a Quality Director who previously ran Halliburton's drilling division, with a master's degree, is executive-level even though he is an employee rather than an owner. Income is met on the affordability test — he paid cash for a $19,000 car and $2,500 for guitar lessons, and the rep's own isolation established that the hesitation was value rather than capacity; the stock-liquidation issue is cash timing, not means. Three things for the rollup. First, the prospect diagnosed the mismatch himself and out loud — 'I didn't see no fat people, you know, that do this' — and was reassured rather than qualified out. Second, this is where the missing clinical criterion becomes concrete rather than theoretical: an ICP built on success, income and starting point has nothing to say about a diagnosed diabetic refusing metformin, and the one screen that mattered does not exist. Third, taken with the rest of the batch, the pattern is now stark — the two core-fit prospects (Andrew Kline, Travis Owen) did not close, and the calls that consumed the most rep time were the ones furthest outside the stated ICP. Whatever the ICP is describing, it is not currently being used to route or disqualify anyone.
